response_text: osYield() cannot be called from within any of the context-switching functions because it interferes with what is used to switch between threads. The osYield() function works by triggering a context switch by setting a specific bit in the ICSR to request the PendSV exception, which is responsible for performing the actual thread switch. However, if osYield() is called from within one of these handlers, the system is already in the middle of handling an interrupt or performing a context switch. Calling osYield() in this state would re-trigger a new context switch before the current one finishes, effectively causing a nested or recursive exception. This leads to undefined behavior, which results in system crashes or hard faults. For this reason, osYield() can only be called by threads running in regular thread mode, not during the execution of exception handlers.\n
